question.text: Per the current NISM XIX-D workbook, a 'Social Impact Fund' (SIF) is a sub-category of which AIF category, and what is its investment thesis?

answer.text: Cat III sub-category; pure listed-equity short-selling
Cat I sub-category; invests in social ventures/social enterprises seeking both financial return and measurable social performance under SEBI's social performance norms
Cat II sub-category; exclusively infrastructure debt
Standalone category outside the SEBI AIF Regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM XIX-D workbook uses "Social Impact Fund (SIF)" — not "Social Venture Fund/SVF" — and places it as a Cat I sub-category alongside Venture Capital Funds, SME Funds, Infrastructure Funds, and Special Situation Funds. SIFs invest in social ventures/social enterprises and are subject to social performance norms; assessment is carried out by Social Impact Assessors. The Trap: "SVF / Social Venture Fund" is a legacy label; the current workbook calls it SIF. Cat III and Cat II categorisations are wrong; "Standalone category" contradicts the SEBI AIF framework. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests Cat I sub-categories at the distributor level; XIX-C/XIX-D test the SIF social-performance-norms framework.
